sources.title: LinuxGSM Game-Server-Configs - Black Mesa full cvar/command dump (status, kick, kickid, banid, banip, listid, listip, removeid, removeip, writeid, writeip, say, motdfile, rcon_password, hostport 27015)
CubeCoders AMP black-mesa.kvp - srcds -game bms -console -usercon -port ..., AdminMethod=SourceRCON, app 346680, config bms/cfg/server.cfg
CubeCoders AMP black-mesaports.json - 27015 'Game and RCON Port'
Black Mesa Admin Commands - Legion Hosting (rcon status, kick <userid>, kick "<name>", banid <minutes> <userid> with 0 = permanent, removeid <steamid>, writeid to banned_user.cfg, say)
How to Create a Dedicated Server for Black Mesa (Deathmatch & Co-op) - Steam guide (server.cfg with rcon_password/hostname/sv_password, port 27015, status, kick, banid)
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community (kick 'by slot, userid or name', banid 'Add a user ID to the ban list', removeid, say)
SourceCoop (Black Mesa Co-op) Admin and Commands Guide - Legion Hosting (Black Mesa admin identity written as STEAM_0:1:12345678 in bms/addons/sourcemod/configs/admins_simple.ini)
SteamDB app 346680 - 'Black Mesa Dedicated Server' (tool); the game itself is app 362890

notes: Black Mesa is srcds with the game directory 'bms', so this is Valve Source RCON over TCP on the game port - 27015 by default (the hostport cvar reads 27015; the port is moved with the -port launch argument). There is no separate RCON port and no enable cvar: putting rcon_password in bms/cfg/server.cfg is what turns RCON on. AMP's template additionally passes -usercon on the srcds command line, which is the usual belt-and-braces for Source servers, so try it if RCON refuses connections. Only vanilla engine commands are recorded - no SourceMod assumed - and each was checked against the server's own cvar/command dump published in LinuxGSM's Game-Server-Configs repo, which lists status ('Display map and connection status'), kick ('Kick a player by name'), kickid ('Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message'), banid, banip, listid, listip, removeid, removeip, writeid ('Writes a list of permanently-banned user IDs to banned_user.cfg'), writeip, say and the motdfile cvar. banid takes MINUTES FIRST and then the identifier, 0 meaning permanent. IMPORTANT: banid and removeid change only the in-memory list - send writeid afterwards or the ban is lost at the next map change; writeid is not folded into the templates because a command here must be a single line. kickid accepts either the numeric userid (captured here as accountId) or the uniqueid, plus a trailing message, which is why {reason} is included; the plain kick command takes a name instead ('kick "{playerName}"'). UNRESOLVED, and worth verifying before trusting unban: no source retrieved shows real Black Mesa status output, so the exact rendering of the uniqueid is unconfirmed. Source engines print either the Steam2 form (STEAM_0:1:12345678) or the Steam3 form ([U:1:25000001]) depending on how new the Steamworks SDK behind the build is, and both are accepted by the pattern and the ban-file pattern here; the practical rule is to pass back the string status printed rather than converting it. Sources also disagree on the ban argument: the Steam dedicated-server guide writes 'banid 0 steamid64', a form vanilla Source banid is not documented to parse, while Legion Hosting writes 'banid <minutes> <userid>'; a SourceCoop admin guide for Black Mesa writes admins as STEAM_0:1:12345678. Steam ID rather than userid was chosen for playerId because removeid and bms/cfg/banned_user.cfg are Steam-ID keyed, so a userid would make unban and ban-file reconciliation impossible - the userid is still captured as accountId for callers that prefer 'kickid <userid>'. say broadcasts to everyone and appears prefixed with 'Console:'. There is no MOTD command - the MOTD is the file named by the motdfile cvar (and motdfile_text for clients with HTML MOTDs disabled) - so motd is omitted. The dedicated server is Steam app 346680, 'Black Mesa Dedicated Server'; the game itself is app 362890.
